cells.tense: You are moving toward something and you can feel all of what it might bring.
cells.ask: Before you start today, say out loud the one thing you're actually going after. Then do that and leave the other maybes alone until it's finished.
cells.core: You're going after something and you can feel everything it might become. That's not scattered. You're holding a lot of possible feelings about where this could land, and you're still moving toward it — which is harder than picking one thing and going blind.\nThe people who do this well feel the whole range and still choose which one drives today. The others don't disappear. They just don't steer. Say the one you're acting on and let the rest wait their turn, because the ones that only passed through will pull you off the road you meant to walk, and by the time you look up you're somewhere you didn't pick.
cells.sheetLine: You can feel it all and still pick the one you're moving on.
cells.verb: gathering every feeling that might be — and acting on one
cells.place: in the push toward a goal

cells.tense: You are living in what this might become, out ahead of anything that has happened yet.
cells.ask: Finish one thing you already started before you begin the next possibility. Set it down when it's done and let it stand.
cells.core: You're moving toward something and you've gone ahead of it. Every feeling this could produce has already been felt and planned for, and the want is outrunning the thing itself.\nThe way this works is that the forward feeling feeds the step you're on. You taste what's coming and it moves the next move. That's not what's happening. The step is somewhere behind you and the appetite for it all is doing the driving. Finish what's in your hands before the next one calls. The want doesn't need to be smaller — it needs the ground under it to stay worth having.
cells.sheetLine: You're at the end of a story you haven't lived yet.
cells.verb: gathering every feeling that might be — and acting on one

cells.tense: You stopped moving toward the thing, and the direction you had went quiet.
cells.ask: Say one thing you want out loud — to someone or to nobody. Small counts. It can be as thin as liking a song.
cells.core: You were moving toward something and you aren't moving toward it now. The direction is there and it isn't pulling, so you stay where you are and wait for a feeling strong enough to go on.\nWhen this is working, a small want is enough to start the next step. You don't need the whole feeling first — one thin pull will take you to the doorway. That's the part that went quiet, not the goal. Wanting one small thing today asks very little of you, and it tells you whether the direction is still in there. Leave the big want alone for now. The small one carries the same line.
cells.sheetLine: The direction is there and it stopped pulling.

cells.tense: You are already pulling people toward what you want, and describing it as something that happened to you.
cells.ask: Name one thing you did today that changed what someone else wanted. Say it as yours, even if it was small.
cells.core: You're moving toward something and people come with you. You pick what to show and when, and it shifts what they feel about the thing. You've been doing this a while and you put it out there as if the pull showed up on its own.\nThe steady version is knowing you're the one who does it, so you can turn it on or leave it off on purpose. That's the whole difference. You don't have to call it a gift. See that the momentum belongs to you, and the feeling you stir becomes something you hold instead of something that holds you.
cells.sheetLine: You're the one pulling, and you've been calling it chance.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the reader is gathering emotional possibilities at all — the record cannot see their life, and someone with one clear feeling and no cloud of choice will read this and shrug. The likely objection is that this sounds like dating advice dressed up as a reading; the ask survives being wrong because acting on one thing today teaches the person where their energy actually goes, whatever the card says. The sentence that serves me is any line about abundance or harvest being intoxicating — it sounds like the map and says nothing the person can use.
